articles.title: WATCH: Nitish Kumar Reddy’s Catch Celebration Turns Awkward After Free-Hit Twist
articles.description: Nitish Reddy Free-Hit Catch: Nitish Kumar Reddy became the centre of an amusing moment during India’s opening T20I against New Zealand after a catch celebration turned into an embarrassing realisation. The Indian all-rounder thought he had helped dismiss Bevon Jacobs, but the situation changed when he recognised that the delivery was a free-hit. The incident unfolded during Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s spell, when Jacobs attempted to launch a full delivery towards the boundary. The New Zealand batsmanfailed to make proper contact, sending the ball towards long-on, where Reddy safely completed the catch. Reddy’s Celebration Quickly Turns Awkward Believing India had secured another wicket, Reddy looked pretty content with the effort, holding on to the ball. However, the excitement did not last long. He soon realised that Jacobs could not be dismissed through a conventional caught-out decision off a free-hit, prompting the all-rounder to acknowledge the mistake and apologise. The sequence provided a light-hearted interruption during an action-packed contest. A free-hit protects the batsmen from being dismissed through several methods such as being caught, bowled or leg before wicket, although certain dismissals, including run-out, remain possible. Abhishek Sharma’s Drop Adds To India’s Fielding Concerns Reddy’s mix-up was not the only fielding incident involving India during the contest. Abhishek Sharma also put down a straightforward chance offered by Daryl Mitchell, giving the New Zealand batter another opportunity at the crease. Mitchell was unable to turn the reprieve into a substantial innings, although he managed to add a couple of boundaries before eventually losing his wicket. The missed opportunity and Reddy’s free-hit confusion once again brought attention to India’s fielding standards. While individual mistakes are part of the game, repeated lapses can become costly in closely fought matches, particularly when opponents are looking to build momentum.

articles.title: Amit Mishra Joins Star-Studded Delhi Capitals Coaching Staff For IPL 2027: Check Full List
articles.description: Delhi Capitals Coaching Staff For IPL 2027: Former India leg-spinner Amit Mishra has joined Delhi Capitals as their spin-bowling coach ahead of IPL 2027, adding another experienced name to the franchise's revamped coaching setup. Mishra joins a group led by former India captain Sourav Ganguly, with Yuvraj Singh and former Sri Lanka pacer Chaminda Vaas also taking up coaching roles. The appointment marks Mishra's return to the Delhi franchise, where his IPL journey began. The 43-year-old retired from all forms of cricket in September 2025 and will now begin his coaching career in the league with the same franchise he represented as a player. Mishra finished his IPL career with 174 wickets and remains the only bowler to have taken three hat-tricks in the tournament's history. His experience in the competition will be an addition to Delhi Capitals' spin-bowling department as the team prepares for the 2027 season. Delhi Capitals Coaching Staff For IPL 2027: Full List Head Coach: Sourav Ganguly Assistant Coach: Yuvraj Singh Fast-Bowling Coach: Chaminda Vaas Spin-Bowling Coach: Amit Mishra Sourav Ganguly To Lead Delhi Capitals' New Coaching Setup Ganguly will take charge as Delhi Capitals' head coach after previously being associated with the franchise in different roles. The former India captain has also coached Pretoria Capitals in South Africa's SA20 league and worked with Delhi Capitals in the Women's Premier League. Yuvraj, meanwhile, will work as assistant and batting coach. The former India all-rounder is beginning his formal coaching career after years of mentoring young Indian players. His appointment reunites him with Ganguly, under whom he played for India. Vaas brings international playing and coaching experience to the pace-bowling department. The former Sri Lanka left-arm fast bowler has worked with Sri Lanka's teams and also held coaching and consultancy roles involving New Zealand and Ireland. Mishra's appointment completes the four-person coaching group outlined above. Delhi Capitals will hope the experience of the former India internationals helps the team prepare for the 2027 campaign as they continue their pursuit of a maiden IPL title.
